candidate.title: Durable Result Identity and Availability Separation
candidate.problemStatement: Systems that reuse durable results across time or location can mistake an immutable result identity, a retention promise, a current availability observation, a transport locator, or prior qualification as proof of the others.
candidate.scope: Incubating cross-domain principle generated from Buildchain v4 Stage Capsule; numbering, cross-domain transfer, independent implementation, production reuse, and universal necessity are not claimed.

observationPerspective.bearer: Buildchain maintainers and agents implementing staged build recovery
observationPerspective.proximity: inside Stage Capsule contract, store, checkpoint, resume, and qualification implementation
consequences: bears false reuse, false rebuild, corrupted restore, provider coupling, and recovery defects

currentOntology: KFD-1 fact cut and welded surface
genesis.observation: Buildchain recovery could not safely treat a digest, retained blob, provider locator, retention policy, or earlier qualification as one cache-hit fact. The successor process needed each coordinate to vary without rewriting the others.
genesis.candidateObject: A portable separation principle may require reusable durable results to keep immutable identity, retention commitment, observed availability, transport coordinates, and qualification independently addressable.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut opens qualification of the separation and does not decide whether it is a new KFD, an existing-KFD composition, a Buildchain Domain Profile, an infrastructure composition, or no new Primitive.

transformedPerspective.bearer: a later process, agent, or operator deciding whether to reuse a durable result
transformedPerspective.role: receiver and consequence bearer for restore or rebuild
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside current purpose, time, availability, and recovery consequences but outside the original execution
consequences: bears unsafe reuse, unnecessary rebuild, unavailable evidence, stale qualification, and hidden custody failure

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from the producer that had just completed a stage to the successor process that must decide whether the result remains reusable after process, time, platform, policy, store, and provider state may have changed.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: The successor needs to reject or permit reuse without inferring availability from identity, identity from location, custody from promise, or current qualification from a historical pass.
genesis.methodNotes: The exact Buildchain cut is founding evidence only. Public prior art and existing KFD composition remain active alternatives.

contactSides: immutable result identity and historical production evidence
a successor receiver observing mutable storage, transport, policy, and purpose conditions
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Systems commonly reconstruct the reuse decision from cache hits, provider IDs, mutable locators, retention configuration, logs, timestamps, and operator knowledge.

pressureChanges.description: Reuse occurs after the producing process and its ambient state have disappeared.
Results move across platforms, stores, providers, processes, and receiver policies.
False reuse can ship incorrect bytes while false rebuild wastes time and scarce compute.
Storage, transport, qualification, and production execution may have different owners.

observedFailures: A provider artifact ID or locator is treated as immutable semantic identity.
A retention policy is treated as proof that bytes are present and intact.
A content digest is treated as proof that content remains retrievable.
Historical qualification is reused after source, platform, toolchain, policy, or purpose drift.
A cache hit silently grants provider or production stage-skipping authority.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: Separating identity, retention, availability, transport, qualification, and reuse assessment may let successors restore or rebuild deterministically without rewriting history or importing provider authority.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: KFD-1, KFD-2, KFD-7, action-cache/CAS contracts, provenance, and adopter-owned storage policy may provide equivalent closure without a new KFD.

pressure: Buildchain v4 required three separate roots for identity, capsule retention, and current availability.
Its store and resume planner keep content, transport, qualification, and provider effects separate.
Six real-runner shadow campaigns and adversarial cases passed at one protected merge cut.
The implementation remains first-party, shadow-only, and production-reuse disabled.
Existing cache and provenance standards already cover major parts of the mechanism.

factSources.observer: Remote Execution and caching prior art

grounding.evidenceBoundary: The cut retains exact public Buildchain contracts, PR review and hosted check outcomes, existing KFD decisions, and bounded public prior art. It contains no independent non-Buildchain implementation, production reuse, non-software transfer, exhaustive prior-art review, or authority-separated terminal KFD disposition.
knownGaps: No independent implementation outside the Buildchain writer code
No production reuse under a bounded rollback gate
No measured cross-domain deletion or fuse witness
No independent exact-cut KFD qualification review
No terminal promotion, subsumption, rejection, or no-new-kfd disposition

alternatives.name: New portable KFD principle
alternatives.reason: The separation may change safe reuse decisions in domains beyond software builds, but no transfer witness exists.

alternatives.name: KFD-1, KFD-2, and KFD-7 composition
alternatives.reason: Non-drifting fact surfaces, fact-bound trust, and visible degraded coordinates may already imply the full responsibility.

alternatives.name: Buildchain Domain Profile
alternatives.reason: Stage Capsule may be a product-specific realization whose exact fields should remain adopter-owned.

alternatives.name: Action cache, CAS, provenance, and retention policy composition
alternatives.reason: Established infrastructure may provide equivalent closure with less normative expansion.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: The current evidence is compatible with a useful explicit composition that deserves no KFD number.

contractModel.identity: A durable result binds exact inputs, transformation, environment or platform boundary, outputs, and referenced qualification roots without mutable provider or transport coordinates.
contractModel.boundary: Result identity, retention commitment, observed availability, transport coordinate, qualification, explicit evaluation cut, and receiver-owned reuse decision remain semantically distinguishable.
contractModel.authority: The principle would not create storage, transport, qualification, provider, production, or receiver authority; each remains independently owned and cited.
contractModel.lifecycle: A result identity remains immutable while commitments, availability observations, transport coordinates, qualifications, and reuse assessments gain successor cuts, expire, degrade, or are revoked without rewriting it.

minimumClosure.notes: Buildchain closes one product model, but the minimum portable vocabulary and optional-coordinate semantics remain unqualified.

deletion.notes: Buildchain fault campaigns demonstrate local pressure, but no non-build fixed-root case shows a changed decision or measured reconstruction burden.

fuse.notes: The product contract varies responsibilities independently, but existing KFD and infrastructure compositions have not been shown insufficient.

falsifiers: Existing KFD decisions and an adopter Profile reproduce every bounded reuse decision at lower total cost.
Action cache, CAS, provenance, and ordinary retention policy supply equivalent closure.
The distinction fails to transfer to a structurally non-build domain.
Independent implementations cannot preserve the separation without importing Buildchain-specific fields.
Production use requires hidden provider identity, ambient state, or fused authority.
The model produces no measurable safety or reconstruction benefit.

dogfood.notes: Buildchain self-dogfood and Kungfu shadow consumers passed three-platform campaigns, but production reuse, independent implementation, and cross-domain transfer were intentionally disabled or absent.

decision.owner: KFD maintainers subject to independent exact-cut review
decision.reason: The founding implementation demonstrates a coherent and consequential separation, while existing KFD and mature infrastructure alternatives prevent promotion without cross-domain deletion, fuse, production, and independent-implementation evidence.
residualRisks: The Candidate may merely restate KFD-1, KFD-2, and KFD-7.
Buildchain terminology may leak into a supposedly portable principle.
First-party shadow evidence may be mistaken for independent or production qualification.
Additional coordinates may increase complexity without changing decisions.
Provider-neutral schemas may still encode build-specific assumptions.
A new KFD could duplicate mature cache, provenance, and custody standards.
